findings.message: The previous round's finding was about a week that crosses the edge of the report range. hoursVisibleTo must count every live entry of that week, as Time's weekProjects does, and not only the entries inside the range. The fix in hours-scope.ts handles this (the class fix is in place), but no test covers it. Every case here uses the range 2026-10-01..2026-10-31 and days in W42 and W44, which sit wholly inside the range. If the old `e.day between from and to` filter came back, every case would still pass. The test also seeds its CON entry with `.catch(() => undefined)`. If that log fails, the W44 'only Contoso Portal' case still returns false, because the week then has no projects, so that case proves nothing. Fix: add a case for a week split by the range edge. Log Fleet Tracker hours for Kasun on a day just before `from` and Contoso hours just after it, in the same ISO week. Assert that Nimal sees the in-range day. Drop the swallowed catch so a failed seed fails the test.
findings.scenario: Revert hours-scope to count only entries with day between from and to. Kasun has FLT hours on Tue 2026-09-29 and CON hours on Thu 2026-10-01 (both W40). With range from=2026-10-01, Nimal should see 2026-10-01 but now does not. The current suite stays green.

findings.message: The project set of a week is now worked out by a third hand-written query. contracts.ts has `weekProjects` (line 60) and weeks.ts has `weekProjectIds`. All three count every live entry of the week, so today they agree. Nothing ties them together, though, so a later change to one (for example how deleted entries or moved entries are counted) won't reach the others. Fix: build this aggregate from the same `weekProjects` SQL fragment, exported from one place.
